notes:
OPHIS v3b: Karpathy's MODEL and OPTIMIZER at 228791f, under an OPHIS benchmark that is NOT Karpathy's benchmark. Read this before comparing any number here to an upstream one.

THIS IS NOT A KARPATHY BASELINE. Three deliberate departures:
(1) PROTOCOL VIOLATION: program.md section 1 states 'Keep prepare.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and baseline provenance sealed and stable; only train.py is the normal mutable path.' OPHIS modifies prepare.py, which the pinned protocol declares immutable and which defines the ground-truth data loader and evaluator.
(2) THE TOKEN CACHE IS NOT NEUTRAL. An earlier version of this note called it a 'throughput change only' because the token stream is byte-identical. That reasoning is WRONG under a wall-clock budget: the budget is 300 charged training SECONDS, so a faster input pipeline buys ~3.76x more optimizer steps and therefore a materially better model. In Karpathy's benchmark, input-pipeline speed IS part of what is being measured. The cache is a legitimate OPHIS scope choice and an illegitimate claim about his benchmark.
(3) DIFFERENT METRIC. Upstream computes token byte lengths via decode([id]).encode('utf-8'); OPHIS uses decode_single_token_bytes(). These are different denominators, so v3b val_bpb and upstream val_bpb are DIFFERENT METRICS and are not comparable in either direction.

Also pinned here: a dedicated corpus root, 10 fixed train shards, and a separately hashed tokenizer with a versioned byte table. Defensible reproducibility, and still a new scope.

NO UPSTREAM REFERENCE NUMBER IS ESTABLISHED IN THIS REPOSITORY. Earlier notes treated val_bpb 0.9912 at 1006 steps / 42% MFU as Karpathy's result; that figure is not backed by any upstream log vendored here and must not be used as a target. Karpathy additionally states results are platform-specific and not comparable across hardware.
